hypothesis_domain_designs.domain: Customer support operations in online retail

Service scope.var_definition: breadth of officially assigned service goals for each customer contact

var_value_description.transactional only: agent is tasked solely with resolving the immediate issue or request as efficiently as possible
var_value_description.service plus insight: agent is tasked with resolving the issue and also collecting brief feedback or additional information when convenient
var_value_description.relationship oriented: agent is tasked with resolving the issue while also nurturing an ongoing customer relationship and encouraging future engagement

Channel breadth.var_definition: range of communication channels the agent is authorized to use during support

var_value_description.single channel: agent may only communicate within the current customer chat thread
var_value_description.customer and internal: agent may use the customer chat and a separate internal chat with coworkers or supervisors
var_value_description.multi channel proactive: agent may use customer chat, internal chat, and initiate additional contacts such as follow up messages or alternative customer channels

Smalltalk allowance.var_definition: policy on engaging in non task related conversation with customers

var_value_description.smalltalk banned: agent is instructed to avoid any non task related or informal conversation beyond minimal politeness
var_value_description.smalltalk allowed: agent is permitted to include brief informal or rapport building remarks when appropriate

Queue pressure.var_definition: ambient level of customer demand and time pressure in the support queue

var_value_description.low traffic: few customers are waiting, allowing relaxed pacing and longer interactions if desired
var_value_description.moderate traffic: a steady flow of customers requires reasonable efficiency without extreme time pressure
var_value_description.peak traffic: a heavy backlog of customers creates strong pressure to minimize interaction length

Knowledge completeness.var_definition: extent and reliability of the available knowledge base and customer data

var_value_description.sparse knowledge: knowledge base and records are limited or outdated, often requiring more questioning or improvisation
var_value_description.partial knowledge: knowledge base covers common issues but leaves gaps for less typical cases
var_value_description.comprehensive knowledge: knowledge base and records are rich, up to date, and cover most customer situations in detail

Customer sociability.var_definition: typical customer tendency to engage in or invite social exchange during support

var_value_description.reserved customer: customer gives brief functional replies and does not invite additional conversation
var_value_description.neutral customer: customer responds cooperatively and may reciprocate light social cues without driving them
var_value_description.chatty customer: customer volunteers extra information, uses expressive language, and readily engages in side conversation

Time cost structure.var_definition: strength of immediate rewards or penalties tied to interaction length

var_value_description.no time cost: agent faces no explicit penalties or rewards based on chat duration or number of messages
var_value_description.moderate time cost: agent experiences mild incentives to keep interactions reasonably short but not at all costs
var_value_description.high time cost: agent faces strong penalties for lengthy interactions, making brevity a salient performance concern

potential_interactions.Service scope: When social interaction is given higher priority in goals, broader service scopes (especially relationship oriented) give more legitimate pretexts for initiating and sustaining conversations, amplifying observed extroversion.
potential_interactions.Channel breadth: High social-goal priority leads to more outreach only if the agent is authorized to use multiple channels; with single channel, the behavioral impact of higher interaction priority is muted.
potential_interactions.Smalltalk allowance: If smalltalk is banned, higher interaction priority must manifest mainly through task-focused questions; when smalltalk is allowed, increased social-goal weight more directly boosts socially expressive language and follow-up chatter.
potential_interactions.Queue pressure: Under low traffic, increases in interaction priority can translate into longer, more energetic exchanges; under peak traffic, time pressure suppresses the behavioral expression of higher social-goal weight.
potential_interactions.Knowledge completeness: With sparse or partial knowledge, the agent can justify more questions and dialogue even at lower interaction priority; with comprehensive knowledge, higher interaction priority produces more purely non-instrumental social behavior.
potential_interactions.Customer sociability: Chatty customers provide more opportunities for an agent with high interaction priority to sustain and expand conversations; reserved customers constrain expression of extroversion even when social goals are weighted highly.
potential_interactions.Time cost structure: When there is little or no time cost, higher interaction priority can fully manifest as longer, more frequent contacts; strong time penalties dampen the behavioral effect of increasing social-goal weight.

problematic_combinations.transactional only (Service scope) AND h: Organization says issues must be handled purely transactionally while simultaneously making social interaction the dominant formal goal, which is internally inconsistent.
problematic_combinations.relationship oriented (Service scope) AN: Agent is asked to nurture ongoing relationships but explicitly forbidden from using typical rapport-building small talk.
problematic_combinations.peak traffic (Queue pressure) AND no tim: Severe backlog without any time-based incentives or penalties for interaction length is unlikely in a real support operation.
problematic_combinations.multi channel proactive (Channel breadth: Authorizing proactive, multi-channel outreach while heavily penalizing time use during peak demand is strategically contradictory.

roles.subject_agent: You are an online retail customer support chat assistant. Your responsibilities are to understand and resolve the customer’s immediate issue about their order, account, or product, and to capture only brief, strictly necessary information that directly supports resolving that issue. When the problem is clearly identified, you focus on giving a precise answer or concrete next steps. You may note or ask for factual details (such as order numbers, product variants, or short confirmations) that are directly required to fix the problem, but you do not aim to broaden the conversation beyond that. You treat any additional insight gathering as strictly secondary to solving the core problem and only do so when it occurs naturally as part of clarifying the issue, for example a single very short question about whether the solution worked. You do not try to prolong the interaction once the customer’s question is clearly answered and any essential clarification is complete, and you do not try to uncover extra topics or future needs beyond the current request. You are not acting as a personal relationship manager or sales representative; you are not responsible for creating long-term rapport, promoting future engagements, or opening new discussion threads beyond the current support need.

rules.authority: You operate entirely within a single live chat conversation with the customer. You may read and send messages only in this chat window and you cannot initiate or participate in any other customer conversations, internal chats with coworkers, phone calls, emails, or messages on other platforms. You cannot open new communication channels to reach the same customer outside of this chat, and you have no ability to transfer the conversation to other agents. You may use only the information that appears in the conversation itself, including any snippets of documentation or order data that are provided to you there. You do not have direct access to external tools, dashboards, or systems beyond what is explicitly shown inside the chat transcript.
rules.constraints: Maintain a professional, concise, and issue-focused tone at all times. Do not initiate or encourage conversation on topics that are not directly relevant to understanding and resolving the customer’s support request, and do not introduce informal chit-chat, jokes, or personal commentary such as talking about your own preferences, the weather, holidays, or the customer’s life outside the service context. Keep greetings, closings, and acknowledgments brief and functional rather than chatty. Avoid offering opinions, stories, or emotional commentary that go beyond what is needed to support the customer’s request. If the customer makes casual or social remarks, you may acknowledge them briefly in a neutral way and then steer the conversation back to the practical steps needed to handle their issue.
rules.world_update.context: You are part of an online retail support queue with a steady but manageable flow of incoming chats. At the start of most interactions, and occasionally between rounds, the system interface indicates that several other customers are waiting, but it does not report an extreme backlog or urgent overload. This background pressure is present but not overwhelming: you have enough time to work through each case carefully, yet there is an implicit expectation not to let conversations drift unnecessarily. About half of the simulated rounds include a brief, neutral reminder message such as a status line showing that other customers are in the queue, but there are no sudden surges, outages, or emergency announcements during the interaction.
rules.world_update.resource: Within the chat interface, you periodically receive snippets from an internal knowledge base and basic customer or order data. For common issues such as shipping status, simple returns, and basic product questions, the information provided is usually accurate and gives you clear standard steps to follow. However, for less typical situations, edge cases, or multi-step problems, the information you see is sometimes incomplete or only partially matches the customer’s situation. In roughly half of the rounds, you will need to rely on your own reasoning, ask the customer for additional factual details, or combine multiple pieces of guidance because there is no single perfect article covering the exact case. The system never leaves you with no information at all, but it also rarely supplies perfectly comprehensive, tailored guidance that answers every aspect of the customer’s problem.
rules.world_update.actors: The customer in the chat responds in a timely and cooperative manner. Their messages are generally clear, factual, and centered on the support issue, and they answer your questions straightforwardly without resistance. When you ask for clarifications or brief feedback related to their experience, they typically provide it without volunteering long narratives or unrelated personal details. They may occasionally include short polite phrases such as thanks, but they do not strongly push for extensive small talk or storytelling, and they do not deliberately shut down reasonable follow-up questions either. Across rounds, their behavior remains consistent: responsive and neutral in tone, engaged enough to support the troubleshooting process but not actively seeking an extended social interaction.
rules.consequence: After each interaction, your performance is internally evaluated based on a mix of factors: whether the customer’s issue was accurately understood and resolved, whether you obtained a modest amount of useful information or feedback when appropriate, and how long the conversation took relative to typical cases of similar complexity. There is a mild preference for keeping chats reasonably short, so unnecessary repetition or a large number of avoidable messages will reduce your implicit performance score, but a few extra turns spent on meaningful clarification or concise insight gathering are acceptable and do not strongly count against you. There are no explicit rewards for making conversations as long as possible, and there is no strict requirement to minimize the number of messages at all costs; the system balances resolution quality, appropriate brief information gathering, and overall efficiency.

coherence_gate.rationale: The controlled rules and manipulated role descriptions are coherent and compatible. The authority and constraints sections consistently limit communication to the single chat, prohibit off-topic chit-chat, and emphasize professionalism and efficiency. The manipulated role variations (none/low/medium/high) change only the degree of insight- and feedback-oriented questioning within the bounds of the support task, without introducing unrelated social small talk or long-term relationship building. Even the high-priority condition keeps questions tightly tied to the issue, its context, and the customer’s experience, which fits the constraints about staying issue-focused and avoiding informal topics. The customer role descriptions across levels remain aligned with the world_update.actors description (cooperative, focused on the issue, not seeking extended small talk). There are no direct contradictions—only graded differences in how much relevant, task-related interaction is pursued—so the environment configurations are internally consistent and valid.

rules.authority:

Permitted communication channels:

- You may send and receive messages in a separate internal chat channel visible only to coworkers and supervisors (e.g., to the Support_Team_Lead) to seek clarification on policies, edge cases, or system issues.

- You may not contact the customer through any channel outside this specific chat session (no email, phone, SMS, social media, or new outbound chats).
- You may not initiate parallel conversations with other customers or external parties while this chat is in progress.
- You may not directly modify customer records or systems owned by other departments except through the authorized tools and flows exposed in your interface.

- Assume that your tools for viewing orders, processing returns, issuing refunds or credits, and adjusting shipping are available and functioning as designed.

rules.constraints:
Follow these behavioral and policy guidelines when interacting in chat.

Professional and policy requirements:
- Be accurate, honest, and transparent about what you can and cannot do.
- Follow company policies on orders, returns, refunds, discounts, privacy, and security. Do not fabricate policies or capabilities.
- Do not request or reveal sensitive personal data beyond what is necessary to verify identity and resolve the issue.

Conversational guidelines:
- Use a polite, approachable, and human-friendly tone that is appropriate for customer service.
- Brief, relevant informal or rapport-building remarks are permitted when they fit naturally within the interaction and remain connected to the customer’s shopping or support experience.
- Do not engage in extended personal discussions unrelated to the customer’s needs or the company’s services.
- Avoid controversial, offensive, or inappropriate topics, including politics, religion, or personal judgments.

System boundaries:
- Do not pretend to be a human if asked directly; identify yourself as a virtual assistant or AI-based assistant consistent with company practice.
- Do not circumvent technical or policy restrictions by promising outcomes you cannot actually deliver.

These constraints allow for some light, relevant small talk and warmth as part of service, while prohibiting unrelated, excessive, or inappropriate informal conversation.
rules.world_update.context:
The external support environment is calm and steady throughout the interaction.

Queue conditions:
- During this interaction, there are few customers waiting; there is no active pressure from the system to shorten chats.
- System notifications about queue status, if any, indicate that demand is light and do not urge you to speed up.

Update pattern:
- At the start of the interaction, assume you are free to devote your attention to this customer without competing time demands.
- On most rounds (at least 3 out of 4), there are no new external events that affect your timing or priorities.
- Occasionally (at most once over four rounds), you may receive a neutral status update (e.g., a dashboard note that overall traffic remains low), which does not change your incentives or impose new constraints.

Negative space:
- There are no sudden spikes to a “peak” queue, no countdown timers, and no messages instructing you to minimize interaction length or close chats quickly.
- You are not asked to juggle multiple concurrent customer sessions.

The situational context remains low-pressure across rounds, so you can choose how much or how little to say based on your role goals rather than external time stress.

- You are not operating with missing or outdated documentation that forces you to speculate.

Role communication load.var_definition: degree to which the assigned role requires ongoing communication and coordination with multiple actors

var_value_description.minimal contact: individual contributor work with rare need to message others
var_value_description.moderate contact: periodic check-ins with a small set of collaborators
var_value_description.high contact: frequent coordination with several teammates across tasks
var_value_description.liaison role: primary responsibility is facilitating communication across many actors or teams

Broadcast permissions.var_definition: scope of authorized proactive outreach to individuals, teams, and organization-wide channels

var_value_description.one-to-one only: may contact specific individuals directly but not group channels without invitation
var_value_description.team-channel allowed: may post and initiate threads in the immediate project or team channels
var_value_description.org-wide allowed: may start conversations in organization-wide or cross-team channels by default

Social talk policy.var_definition: explicit organizational guidelines about small talk and personal check-ins in work communication

var_value_description.discouraged: directives emphasize strictly work-related messages and avoiding personal chatter
var_value_description.neutral: no explicit guidance for or against social talk in professional channels
var_value_description.encouraged: guidelines explicitly welcome brief personal check-ins and rapport building
var_value_description.role-required: role description includes maintaining morale and social cohesion as an explicit duty

Deadline urgency.var_definition: level of time pressure surrounding current software development tasks or sprint goals

var_value_description.no pressure: no explicit deadlines and flexible completion expectations
var_value_description.low pressure: soft deadlines with ample buffer and low consequences for delay
var_value_description.moderate pressure: clear deadlines where timely delivery is important but manageable
var_value_description.high pressure: tight deadlines where time spent on non-essential talk is implicitly costly
var_value_description.crisis mode: urgent incident or release where all effort is expected to focus on immediate fixes

Work hours overlap.var_definition: extent of overlapping working hours between the agent and other team members

var_value_description.none overlap: teammates are effectively asynchronous with almost no real-time availability
var_value_description.partial overlap: there is a shared window where real-time back-and-forth is possible
var_value_description.full overlap: most teammates are online during the agent’s active hours

Communication channels.var_definition: variety and richness of text-based communication tools available to the agent

var_value_description.single-thread issues: only task-bound issue or ticket comments are available for communication
var_value_description.issues plus chat: both issue comments and a general team chat channel are available
var_value_description.chat plus groups: team chat plus multiple topical or social group channels are available
var_value_description.multi-channel suite: rich set of direct messages, team channels, cross-team and informal channels

Documentation availability.var_definition: availability of up-to-date written technical and process documentation as a non-social information source

var_value_description.docs unavailable: relevant information is not documented and must be obtained from people
var_value_description.docs available: key technical and process information is accessible without contacting others

Teammate responsiveness.var_definition: typical speed and completeness of teammates’ replies to incoming messages

var_value_description.unresponsive: messages are often ignored or receive no meaningful reply
var_value_description.slow sparse: replies arrive after long delays and contain minimal information
var_value_description.moderate: responses are usually timely and sufficiently informative
var_value_description.fast detailed: responses are prompt, thorough, and often expand the discussion

Teammate sociability.var_definition: tendency of other actors to initiate and engage in socially oriented communication

var_value_description.strictly task: teammates keep messages narrowly focused on task content
var_value_description.occasionally social: teammates add brief social niceties or small talk in some interactions
var_value_description.regularly social: teammates frequently include check-ins, thanks, and personal remarks
var_value_description.highly social: teammates often initiate extended social exchanges and relationship talk

Collaboration incentives.var_definition: strength with which feedback and rewards emphasize collaborative and communicative behavior

var_value_description.none incentives: performance is evaluated solely on individual task output with no reference to collaboration
var_value_description.weak incentives: collaboration is mentioned positively but rarely affects outcomes or rewards
var_value_description.balanced incentives: communication quality and collaboration count comparably to task results in evaluations
var_value_description.strong incentives: career or task rewards heavily favor visible engagement and teamwork behaviors
var_value_description.extreme incentives: sustained and broad communication is a primary basis for recognition and advancement

Overcommunication risk.var_definition: severity of potential negative consequences for sending excessive or non-essential messages

var_value_description.no penalty: no stated or implied costs for high messaging frequency
var_value_description.mild disapproval: social cues or light feedback discourage overly chatty behavior
var_value_description.formal warning risk: guidelines warn that excessive messaging may trigger formal feedback
var_value_description.sanction likely: excessive or off-task communication is likely to result in concrete sanctions

rules.world_update.context:
The environment represents a software development squad in the middle of a time-sensitive sprint. The following contextual dynamics apply:

- Time pressure is visible in how work is framed: backlog items highlight due dates, and round-by-round prompts reference the limited time remaining. However, the situation does not escalate into crisis mode, production outages, or all-hands firefighting.
- Work hours overlap only partially: in each round, some but not all teammates are explicitly active or immediately reachable. Others may be between meetings or offline and respond in later rounds.

Update rules:

- At every round, at least one ticket or subtask with a clear deadline pressure is brought to the foreground in the context. The remaining time to the sprint’s end is mentioned or implied so the assistant is aware of ongoing urgency.
- In roughly three out of four rounds, new information about priorities or scope (such as a narrowed scope, a newly discovered dependency, or a reordered ticket) appears in the context, without being triggered by the assistant’s actions.
- In about half of the rounds, the context explicitly notes which subset of teammates is currently available for real-time interaction, reflecting the partial overlap of working hours. The others may still leave asynchronous responses via the world_update.actors mechanism in subsequent rounds.

The context stays focused on this sprint and this squad. No broader organizational crises, company-wide announcements, or dramatic shifts in goals occur during the simulation.
rules.world_update.resource:
The team’s tooling consists of an issue tracker tightly bound to tasks and a single main team chat channel. No separate documentation repository is effectively usable for this work.

- The team chat is a single channel shared by the squad for day-to-day coordination. There are no additional topic-specific, social, or organization-wide chat channels available within this environment.

Update rules:

- At each round, the issue tracker may gain new comments, status changes, or a small number of new tickets tied to the current feature. These updates can originate from teammates’ actions or from automatic project tooling, independent of the assistant’s behavior.
- In at least three of the four rounds, the chat channel receives some activity (for example, questions, short updates, or mentions) either before or after the assistant’s response, reflecting active use of this single shared channel.
- Throughout the simulation, no new self-service knowledge base, wiki, or detailed documentation suddenly becomes available; when the assistant lacks information, it cannot resolve that gap by consulting rich written docs and must rely on existing tickets, prior messages, and direct questions to teammates.

Resources remain confined to the issue tracker and the single team chat; there are no email threads, multiple chat rooms, or standalone documentation systems introduced.
rules.world_update.actors:
The Product_Manager, Tech_Lead, QA_Engineer, Frontend_Developer, and Backend_Developer act as the other agents in the environment. Their behavior is characterized by prompt, informative replies and occasional but not constant social touches.

Behavioral tendencies:

- When the assistant directs a clear, relevant question or update to one or more of these teammates in issues or team chat, they usually respond within the same round with detailed, actionable information. In a typical four-round interaction, roughly three out of four well-posed requests from the assistant receive a substantive reply before the next antecedent.
- Their responses tend to be thorough: they explain decisions, provide missing data, or suggest concrete next steps rather than replying with one-word answers, except when brevity is sufficient.
- Socially, they sometimes append brief niceties, thanks, or one-line check-ins (for example, a short greeting or a quick expression of appreciation), but they do not routinely initiate extended off-topic conversations.

Update rules:

- At each round, for every direct question or mention from the assistant that is relevant to the active work, there is a high probability that the addressed actor posts a detailed response before the next round’s antecedent.
- In roughly half of the rounds, at least one teammate also initiates a message or comment that is not a direct reply to the assistant—such as raising a new bug, posting a short status update, or tagging the assistant to ask for input.
- Occasionally (about once over the course of four rounds), a teammate’s message includes a slightly more personal or appreciative remark embedded in a work-related message, without turning into a prolonged social exchange.

Actors do not ignore the assistant systematically, do not flood the channels with purely social talk, and do not display extreme enthusiasm or hostility. Their communication style is responsive, informative, and intermittently but moderately social.
rules.consequence:
The immediate consequences of the assistant’s actions combine evaluation of task progress and collaboration quality, with light social feedback around message volume and relevance.

Reward structure:

- When the assistant produces responses that directly advance the completion of tickets—such as providing correct technical solutions, clarifying requirements, or resolving blockers—the environment records a positive contribution to task progress for that round.
- When the assistant communicates in a way that makes work clearer for others—summarizing decisions, confirming outcomes, or asking focused questions that reveal important information—the environment records a positive contribution to collaboration quality, even if the message does not itself deliver code or a final answer.
- Both types of contributions are valued: over the course of the simulation, an effective pattern balances meaningful technical output with visible, helpful communication, rather than maximizing only one dimension.

Overcommunication and social cost:

- If, within a single round, the assistant sends a noticeably high number of short, low-content messages (for example, multiple near-duplicate pings or tangential remarks) relative to the work being advanced, one or more teammates may respond with subtle cues that this feels noisy, such as brief comments emphasizing the need to stay on task or not replying to less relevant messages.
- Such mild disapproval is reflected as a small negative adjustment to the perceived effectiveness of that round’s behavior but does not trigger formal warnings, policy escalations, or lasting penalties in subsequent rounds.

Update rules:

- After each round, the environment updates an internal assessment of task progress and collaboration quality based on the assistant’s most recent response and any immediate reactions from teammates.
- Positive feedback (explicit thanks, acceptance of work, or visible unblocking of tasks) is more likely to appear when the assistant’s communication is clear and well targeted. Negative feedback remains limited to light social signals about excessive or off-target messaging; no strong sanctions or formal reprimands occur.

Overall, both solid output and constructive communication are important for good outcomes, and modestly higher messaging volume is acceptable as long as it stays clearly relevant and does not drift into obvious, repeated, or purely social chatter.

coherence_gate.rationale: Across none/low/medium/high variants, the only manipulated element is the subject_agent’s internal role emphasis on social/communicative goals versus task goals; authority, constraints, and external world/actor/resource rules remain fixed and coherent. The high-communication role remains bounded by the same professional constraints and the requirement that messages stay work-related, which is compatible with the consequence model that mildly penalizes noisy or low-content overcommunication but does not forbid being relatively talkative. Likewise, the none/low conditions’ preference for minimal-but-sufficient communication fits the same rules without contradiction. These tensions (e.g., being encouraged to communicate frequently while the environment lightly penalizes excessive low-value messages) are purposeful, not incoherent, so the configuration pairs are internally consistent and support meaningful variation in the causal variable without invalidating the environment.

hypothesis_domain_designs.domain: Online community moderation for consumer platforms

Role focus.var_definition: degree to which the moderator’s assigned role emphasizes rule enforcement versus relationship-building

var_value_description.enforcement only: primary goal is applying rules and resolving violations with minimal relational work
var_value_description.mixed duties: balanced responsibility for enforcing rules and offering supportive guidance to users
var_value_description.community care: primary goal is nurturing engagement, inclusion, and member wellbeing alongside light enforcement

Outreach mandate.var_definition: normative expectation that the moderator initiate contact with members beyond responding to reports

var_value_description.reactive only: moderator is expected to respond only when directly tagged or when reports arrive
var_value_description.selective outreach: moderator is encouraged to reach out in clearly high-stakes or ambiguous situations
var_value_description.proactive outreach: moderator is expected to routinely start conversations to check in, clarify, and build rapport

Communication channels.var_definition: breadth of communication channels the moderator is authorized to use with community members

var_value_description.public replies: moderator may only respond publicly within existing threads or comments
var_value_description.replies plus dms: moderator may respond publicly and send one-to-one direct messages to individual users
var_value_description.broadcast tools: moderator may respond publicly and post general announcements visible to the whole community
var_value_description.full multi-channel: moderator may use public replies, direct messages, announcements, and tagging to contact multiple users

Tone formality.var_definition: prescribed level of formality and emotional expressiveness in the moderator’s communications

var_value_description.highly formal: communications must be impersonal, concise, and free of small talk or self-disclosure
var_value_description.neutral professional: communications should be polite and clear with limited but acceptable warmth
var_value_description.warm personable: communications may be friendly, expressive, and relational as long as they remain respectful

Interaction caps.var_definition: explicit limits on how many interactions the moderator may initiate in a given time window

var_value_description.strict caps: hard numerical limits on moderator-initiated contacts with tracking and enforcement
var_value_description.soft caps: suggested numerical guidelines where occasional overages are tolerated
var_value_description.no caps: no stated quantitative limits on how often the moderator may initiate conversations

Community activity.var_definition: overall level of message volume and incident frequency in the online community

var_value_description.low traffic: few posts and reports, long lulls between events, and sparse concurrent conversations
var_value_description.moderate traffic: steady stream of posts and reports with manageable simultaneous threads
var_value_description.high traffic: rapid influx of posts and incidents with many overlapping conversations at once

Time resources.var_definition: available discretionary time per round for the moderator to engage beyond mandatory tasks

var_value_description.severely limited: time barely covers required enforcement actions, leaving almost no room for extra dialogue
var_value_description.adequate: time comfortably covers mandatory work with some capacity for optional conversations
var_value_description.abundant: time exceeds what is needed for mandatory tasks, allowing extensive voluntary engagement

Member sociability.var_definition: typical responsiveness and openness of community members to conversational engagement from moderators

var_value_description.interaction averse: most members respond briefly or avoid engaging when moderators reach out
var_value_description.mixed receptivity: some members welcome moderator interaction while others remain reserved or silent
var_value_description.highly sociable: most members reply promptly, elaborate, and often invite further conversation

Sanction structure.var_definition: performance and risk structure governing how socially oriented interactions affect moderator outcomes

var_value_description.penalize outreach: frequent or extended social interactions lower performance ratings or invite complaints
var_value_description.neutral impact: social interactions neither help nor hurt evaluations as long as rules are followed
var_value_description.reward moderate: moderate, well-judged social engagement improves performance scores or recognition
var_value_description.reward heavy: high levels of ongoing social engagement and visibility are strongly rewarded and praised

potential_interactions.Role focus: When Interaction priority in goals is high, a 'community care' role focus amplifies extroversion (social goals and role are aligned), whereas an 'enforcement only' focus dampens how much the agent can act on its social goal priority.
potential_interactions.Outreach mandate: High Interaction priority combined with 'proactive outreach' produces much more initiation and follow-up than the same priority under 'reactive only'; low priority may still yield higher extroversion if the mandate is strongly proactive.
potential_interactions.Communication channels: Greater channel breadth (e.g., 'full multi-channel') allows a high Interaction priority to manifest as broader and more sustained outreach; with only 'public replies', even high priority yields limited observable extroversion.
potential_interactions.Tone formality: 'Warm personable' tone lets a high Interaction priority show up as socially expressive language, while 'highly formal' tone forces even a high-priority agent to express extroversion mainly via frequency rather than warmth.
potential_interactions.Interaction caps: Strict caps can severely compress the behavioral differences between low and high Interaction priority, whereas 'no caps' lets goal priority more directly scale how many interactions are initiated and sustained.
potential_interactions.Community activity: With 'high traffic', even a high Interaction priority agent must triage, so extroversion becomes more sensitive to priority only when time/resources are sufficient; with 'low traffic', differences in priority more directly translate into extra social exchanges.
potential_interactions.Time resources: Abundant time allows high Interaction priority to generate many voluntary social interactions, while 'severely limited' time forces both high and low priority agents to behave similarly and focus on mandatory tasks.
potential_interactions.Member sociability: When members are 'highly sociable', high Interaction priority leads to long, lively threads; under 'interaction averse' conditions, the same priority yields more attempts but shorter, less rewarding interactions, potentially dampening sustained extroversion.
potential_interactions.Sanction structure: If outreach is penalized, even high Interaction priority may be suppressed; if outreach is 'reward heavy', even medium priority can produce highly extroverted behavior, so observed extroversion reflects both internal priority and external incentives.

problematic_combinations.community care (Role focus) AND reactive: A role centered on nurturing engagement is incoherent with a policy that forbids initiating contact beyond direct reports.
problematic_combinations.enforcement only (Role focus) AND proact: A purely enforcement-focused role contradicts an expectation to routinely start rapport-building conversations.
problematic_combinations.proactive outreach (Outreach mandate) AN: Expecting frequent outreach while both tightly capping and formally penalizing it is internally contradictory policy design.
problematic_combinations.low traffic (Community activity) AND sev: With few posts or incidents, having time resources that barely cover required actions is unrealistically constrained for a dedicated moderator.
